tools.name: timestamp_sha256
tools.description: Records the earliest time this platform saw a SHA-256 and returns a signed receipt. Compute the hash yourself; never send the content. Stamping the same hash again returns the first receipt.

tools.name: get_timestamp
tools.description: Returns the signed receipt of a SHA-256 stamped earlier and the state of its daily OpenTimestamps anchor.

tools.name: verify_certificate
tools.description: Checks a PoF-X Maritime certificate by the number printed on it (32 to 64 hex digits): signature, files, a replay by the platform's kernel, and the records with their verdicts.

tools.name: list_rule_packs
tools.description: The public, sealed rule packs of the PoF-X kernel (maritime: MARPOL, FuelEU, EU ETS, CII and more): fields with units and ranges, and every rule with its limit and legal citation. Optional query words filter them.

tools.name: check_rules
tools.description: A deterministic verdict (admit, reject, no-verdict) from the PoF-X kernel for each record, the margin of every rule and its legal citation. Same input, same answer, every time. Free within a daily limit (more with a free API key sent as Authorization: Bearer). Records are objects of field values as

tools.name: lint_pack
tools.description: Runs the kernel's certify and pack-facts on a pack you send (base64): whether it is well formed and sealed, its grade and tier, and every problem the kernel finds. Free.

tools.name: replay_verify
tools.description: Re-derives a chain from a pack and records (all base64) and says whether it matches, byte for byte. With the expect file the result is authenticated. Free.

tools.name: stamp_batch
tools.description: Puts up to 10000 SHA-256 values under one time stamp (a Merkle root) and returns a proof for each, so any one item can later be shown alone. Free.

tools.name: seal_pack
tools.description: Runs the kernel's seal on a pack you send (base64) and returns the sealed pack (base64) and its sha256: after sealing, any change to the pack is detected by the kernel. Free.

tools.name: check_conflicts
tools.description: Decides in exact rational arithmetic whether the rules of a pack (base64) still admit some value on every field, or whether no record can ever be admitted; also one field id with two units. Free.

tools.name: stamp_conversation
tools.description: Hashes a conversation (a list of {role, content}, or one text) in a fixed canonical form and time-stamps the hash. The conversation is not stored; anyone holding the same messages can recompute the hash. Free.

tools.name: record_correction
tools.description: Links a new hash as the correction of an earlier stamp made with the same API key; the link is itself time-stamped. Needs the key (Authorization: Bearer). Free.

tools.name: get_corrections
tools.description: Every correction linked to a time-stamped hash, with the time of each link. Free.

tools.name: request_api_key
tools.description: Makes a free API key at once, without e-mail or account: it raises the daily limit of check_rules to 1000 and lets you correct your own stamps later. Shown once. 3 keys a day per address. The answer includes the getting-started guide (guide_url) and quick steps: read them before using the key. Free.

tools.name: register_publication
tools.description: For a text you have published at a public https address (your site or an archive such as Zenodo or arXiv): time-stamps the text's SHA-256 and a statement naming the address, so the publication has a provable date as prior art. The text is never sent; the address is not opened. Free.

tools.name: get_publication
tools.description: The publication records of a hash: the address named and the time of each record. Free.

tools.name: inspect_ots
tools.description: Reads a .ots proof (base64), recomputes every hash step and lists its attestations: for Bitcoin the block height and the merkle root that block must have; for a pending proof the calendar. No network is used. Free.

tools.name: generate_test_cases
tools.description: For a public rule pack: records at, just below and just above every limit, and at the ends of each field's range. Inputs only; send them to check_rules for the verdicts. Free.

tools.name: check_own_pack
tools.description: Run the PoF-X kernel on a rule pack you wrote (the open pack language: https://platform.ethtopology.com/pack-language.txt). Give pack_text (or pack, base64) and records (objects of field values). The kernel certifies the pack, seals it and returns per record ADMIT, REJECT or NOVERDICT, the margin B

tools.name: request_kernel
tools.description: Asks Novalith Holdings OU for the full kernel in a private build, to run inside your own silicon, device, vehicle or servers. Recorded and answered by e-mail. Try your packs with check_own_pack first.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "request_api_key" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: stamp_conversation · Private data: timestamp_sha256, verify_certificate, check_rules, replay_verify, check_conflicts, record_correction, request_api_key, get_publication, generate_test_cases, check_own_pack, request_kernel · Public sink: timestamp_sha256, lint_pack, seal_pack, generate_test_cases · Destructive: check_own_pack, request_kernel.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: stamp_conversation · Private data: timestamp_sha256, verify_certificate, check_rules, replay_verify, check_conflicts, record_correction, request_api_key, get_publication, generate_test_cases, check_own_pack, request_kernel · Public sink: timestamp_sha256, lint_pack, seal_pack, generate_test_cases · Destructive: check_own_pack, request_kernel

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
